title: Ways of exercising democracy
competency: Explain direct and indirect democracy and the difference between them.

keywords.def: All adult citizens take part in decisions themselves, without elected officials in between.
Citizens elect representatives who decide on their behalf. Also called representative democracy.
A vote in which all citizens decide a specific question directly.

en.text: In direct democracy all adult citizens take part in decisions themselves. They attend meetings, vote, and accept the majority decision. It works in schools, local committees and associations, and through referendums. A whole nation cannot meet together, so it cannot replace representation.

screens.title: Class vote
screens.ask: Your class elects its representative by everyone voting. Who made the decision?
screens.after: The students decided directly. This is a form of direct democracy.

screens.title: Two ways of exercising democracy
paras: There are two ways: direct (pure) and indirect (representative) democracy.
Direct democracy lets all adult citizens take part in decisions without elected officials.

screens.title: 3.1.1 Direct democracy
paras: Every citizen over a certain age may attend political meetings and vote.
They accept the majority decision, even if they voted against it.
Everyone has the right to run for political office.

screens.title: Where it works
paras: A nation's people cannot all gather to make decisions. So direct democracy cannot replace representation.
It works in local committees, schools and citizen associations.
A referendum lets all citizens vote directly on a specific point.

screens.title: Key words
defs: All adult citizens take part in decisions themselves, without elected officials in between.
A vote in which all citizens decide a specific question directly.

screens.text: Is it possible to use direct democracy for every political decision of a country?
opts: No, the whole nation cannot gather for complex issues
screens.ans: No, the whole nation cannot gather for complex issues
screens.why: Direct democracy works in local committees, schools and referendums, not for complex national issues.
screens.clue: Can millions of people meet every day?

screens.text: In direct democracy, you accept the majority decision even if you voted against it.
screens.why: Accepting the majority decision is part of direct democracy.

screens.text: Residents vote on whether their zone becomes a region. What is this vote called?
screens.why: A referendum is a direct consultation of all citizens on a specific point.

opts: All members of the school club vote on the club's trip
MPs pass a law in parliament
A minister decides a new road
screens.ans: All members of the school club vote on the club's trip
screens.why: Every member decides personally, without representatives. The other two are decisions by officials.
screens.clue: Who decides: everyone, or chosen officials?

en.text: In indirect democracy citizens elect representatives who decide for them. In Ethiopia people elect members of the House of Peoples' Representatives every five years. If representatives perform poorly, the people can remove them. Most countries use it today because of population size, distance, resources and time.

screens.title: Too many to meet
screens.ask: Ethiopia has over 100 million people. How can they all make the country's laws?
opts: All meet in one hall every day
They elect representatives to make laws for them
screens.after: They elect representatives. This is indirect (representative) democracy.

screens.title: 3.1.2 Indirect (representative) democracy
paras: This is the type of modern democracy we have today.
Citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf.

screens.title: An example from Ethiopia
paras: Every five years, Ethiopians elect members of Parliament.
They meet in the House of Peoples' Representatives and pass bills that become law.
If they fail to perform, the people can remove them. So the people control their representatives.

screens.title: Direct and indirect
screens.note: REMEMBER: In direct democracy citizens decide by proposing laws or referendums. Indirect democracy relies on a small group of officials.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Citizens elect representatives who decide on their behalf. Also called representative democracy.

screens.text: In a representative democracy, the people of a state have a direct say in all political matters.
screens.why: They act through their elected representatives.

screens.text: How often do Ethiopians elect members of the House of Peoples' Representatives?
screens.why: The book says every five years.

screens.title: Direct or indirect?
items: Students vote for their class representative
A regional council decides a budget
screens.why: Direct: citizens decide. Indirect: representatives decide.

screens.text: Why is indirect democracy preferred in modern times?
opts: Population size, distance, resources and time make direct democracy hard
Citizens are not allowed to vote
screens.ans: Population size, distance, resources and time make direct democracy hard
screens.why: The summary lists population size, topography, resources and time.
screens.clue: Think of a country with millions of people.

screens.text: An MP stops meeting voters and ignores their needs. What can the people do in an indirect democracy?
opts: Vote him out at the next election
screens.ans: Vote him out at the next election
screens.why: If representatives fail to perform, the people have the power to remove them. This is how people control representatives.
screens.clue: Who gave the MP his job?

test.text: Citizens elect representatives to decide for them. This is:
test.why: Representatives decide on the people's behalf.

test.text: A vote where all citizens decide one question directly is a:
Direct democracy works well in local committees and schools.
test.why: The book names local committees, schools and citizen associations.

test.ask: Ethiopians elect members of Parliament every ___ years.

test.text: Why can't a whole nation use only direct democracy?
opts: The people cannot all gather for every complex issue
test.ans: The people cannot all gather for every complex issue
test.why: Size, distance, resources and time make it impossible.
